overall_comments: Pair 03 (L3 'Where Is It?' covering A9.3 + A9.6) clears the bar on every category. The expanded_walkthrough names the over-everything position-word generalisation and grounds the repair in Clements & Sarama (2009) spatial reasoning trajectory, Levine et al. (2012) on spatial language exposure, and Pruden, Levine & Huttenlocher (2011) on embodied placement — recovery_moves are properly 3-way diagnostic-branched (A: one word for everything → fan card forced differentiation; B: knows above/below/beside but mixes inside/outside/between → hula-hoop embodied placement; C: reverses words → paired contrast placements with gesture anchor). Sammy's NAME-IT/SIDES/CORNERS refrain recurs in BOTH bookends (minds_on + consolidation chant 3x with claps), and Mira anchors the positional content with a sentence frame children carry into the worksheet. Duration is realistic at 35 min (7/20/8) — squarely inside the K window. Materials are everyday (chart paper, index cards, paper map, animal tokens) with Sammy/Mira puppets explicitly OPTIONAL, and the differentiation includes a true NO-PAPER, NO-PURCHASE PATH where children physically place themselves above/below/beside/inside (hula-hoop)/outside/between (two classmates) — runnable with zero prep. Worksheet's three parts each map cleanly to a named success criterion (Part 1 = pick from 4 pictures; Part 2 = place 4 animals on map; Part 3 = transfer task with classroom items via 'The ___ is ___ the ___' frame plus a 6-word reference box for ELL/emergent writers). Part 3 is the deliberate transfer-format variation. Math authenticity: vocabulary used precisely, embodied placement (Pruden et al.), children invent their own descriptions in Station C and the exit routine. Advance to pair 04.
